rows.row_extraction: single CSV (econdb.com/static/help/main_tickers.csv, helpers.py:431) read via pandas read_csv, filtered/sorted then DataFrame.to_dict(records)
rows.notes: aextract_data (models/available_indicators.py:91) delegates wholly to helpers.download_indicators; rows are the ticker roster, not an indicator-data message. Derives symbol_root by string surgery (helpers.py:456-463), drops obsolete OECD/underscore tickers (helpers.py:451-454), fixes bad multipliers (478-479), sorts by last_date desc (available_indicators.py:94). Unlike OECD siblings this roster is a static CSV file, no SDMX. C92 upstream read: fillna("N/A").replace("N/A", None).replace("nan", None) runs before sort_values(by=last_date, ascending=False) (helpers.py:481-482; available_indicators.py:94), so a sort over raw text would rank the sentinels. No cap.

rows.row_extraction: 13 parallel get_context() calls per country to /series/context/?tickers=[SYM~TRANSFORM]; each reply's dataarray (helpers.py:534) becomes a date-indexed column, 13 columns concat on axis=1 per country (country_profile.py:257-274), reset_index records; countries chunked 3 at a time
rows.notes: No single profile endpoint exists: the row is assembled across 13 indicator requests (GDP TUSD, RGDP TPOP/TOYA, POP, CPI, CORE, RETA, IP, POLIR, Y10YD, GDEBT TUSD, CA TPGP, URATE). Govt Debt/GDP is divided from two fetched series client-side (country_profile.py:280-282); percent fields /100 in the validator (106-108). Differs from OECD's one-CSV-per-model shape entirely.

rows.row_extraction: two branches. Regular: token bootstrap GET /user/create_token/ (economic_indicators.py:209), then one GET /api/series/?ticker=[combos]&from=&to= whose results[] page is walked via response['next'] links (325-329); each series' data.dates/data.values parallel arrays renamed to date/value rows (452-457) and concat'd. 'main' branch: GET /trends/country_forecast/ then one GET /trends/get_topic_children/ per parent row (main_indicators.py:115-120,146-150), children rows spliced below parents, wide indicator×date frame melted to records
rows.notes: UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: next_link_pagination —— the loop follows a server-returned absolute 'next' URL (line 326); body_offset_pagination is the closest existing key but this is a GET cursor link, not an offset in a request body. Symbol×country×transform combinations are built client-side (helpers.parse_symbols / HAS_COUNTRIES); URL >2000 chars is rejected rather than chunked (312-316); percent values /100 at 466-467.

rows.row_extraction: one GET per country to /widgets/top-trade-items/data/?country=X&split_by=country (export_destinations.py:77); take plots[0].data item dicts, merge plots[0] meta (title/footnote/series[0].code) into every row, rename keys Country->destination_country and 'Value million USD'->value (98-126); results just extended, no cross-request join
rows.notes: This is a website widget JSON, not SDMX — nothing like the OECD trade models. Country names round-trip through the reverse COUNTRY_MAP (param_value_mapping at 66/119); zero-valued and falsy keys are dropped per row (124-125); a ContentTypeError on one country is only fatal when it is the sole country (82-86).

rows.row_extraction: 3 parallel get_context() calls per country to /series/context/ (GDP level [+TUSD unless US], GDP~TPOP, GDP~TOYA, gdp_nominal.py:136-145); each dataarray -> date-indexed column renamed value/nominal_growth_qoq/nominal_growth_yoy, concat on axis=1 keyed by date+Country (164-167), reset_index records
rows.notes: parse_context (helpers.py:579-593) annualizes quarterly GDP by rolling(4).sum for all countries outside GDP_ADJUST and rescales to $B — that derivation is part of the value semantics; US skips the TUSD transform (gdp_nominal.py:140, same-path param branch); growth percents /100 (211-212); date range is filtered after fetch in transform_data (198-201).

rows.row_extraction: identical mechanics to GdpNominal but on the RGDP flow: 3 parallel /series/context/ calls (RGDP [+TUSD unless US], RGDP~TPOP, RGDP~TOYA, gdp_real.py:136-145), dataarray columns renamed value/real_growth_qoq/real_growth_yoy, axis=1 concat on date+Country
rows.notes: Per-row difference from GdpNominal: symbol root RGDP, output fields real_growth_qoq/real_growth_yoy (gdp_real.py:84-91), and country 'all' resolves against INDICATOR_COUNTRIES['RGDP'] (gdp_real.py:54) so the available country set differs. Same rolling(4).sum annualization + $B rescale in helpers.parse_context; same post-fetch date filter and /100 growth scaling (210-212).

rows.row_extraction: one GET of https://www.econdb.com/static/openbb/shipping.json (port_volume.py:81); payload is {Ports:[roster], measure:[{Date,<locode>:value},...]} — for each port code the measure dicts are exploded into {date,port,measure,value} rows (116-130) then pivot_table turns measure columns into import/export TEU + dwell-time fields (146-159)
rows.notes: No per-port request fanout unlike every other econdb model — a single static JSON blob whose Ports roster is joined to rows by locode dict lookups (port_volume.py:111-114, response_dict_keying); measure strings renamed via cols_map (153-158); iso2->country name via reverse COUNTRY_MAP (160-162); start/end dates enforced client-side (165-169) and validator rejects dates before 2022-04-03 (21-29). | C95: :146-152 pivot_table(index=[date,port_code,port_name,country], columns='measure', values='value') melts long INTO wide keyed by document-published measure names; the shipped pivots transpose a STATIC series_keys tuple the other way (row_expansion.py:313, :552), so series_pivot -> path.explode credited a PRESENT capability. :160-161 maps the country code table in reverse.

rows.row_extraction: token bootstrap /user/create_token/ when no key (yield_curve.py:89-93), then one GET /api/series/?ticker=[maturity symbols]&page_size=50 per country; per series data.dates/data.values arrays are folded into a maturity×date frame, rows nearest each requested date kept (209-218), then melted to {date,maturity,rate} records per country (221-236)
rows.notes: Maturity symbol set is per-country from COUNTRIES_DICT (utils/yield_curves.py), not a query echo. Not paged: page_size=50 fixed and no next-link loop (contrast with EconomicIndicators). 'date_window_filter' is a stretch label for nearest-date-per-requested-date selection (209-218): UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: nearest_date_selection —— existing filter keys do not describe snapping to the closest observation. Rates /100 (230).
